correctness.rationale: The source residual polynomial factors exactly as d^2 F_+ F_- with the displayed algebraic constants. Each factor is irreducible over C(v)[t]: its q-discriminant is a nonsquare multiple of A^3, and the remaining fourth-root extension is controlled by the coprime square-free factors H_+,H_- of A; the prospective square root changes sign under the nontrivial automorphism over C(v)(sqrt(A)). Both factors have the same F3 transition and multiplicity four at the six blown-up boundary points, hence each has half the source divisor class. Their resultant is a nonzero constant times B^4 J; after the blow-ups remove the B-boundary coincidence, the 24 simple roots of J give 96 common t-points, equal to the intersection product, so all are transverse. The factor discriminants allocate 32 of the source's ordinary cusps to each factor. Adjunction and delta=1 for ordinary cusps give normalization genus 9.

value.rationale: The residual discriminant is a central geometric object in the initiating paper: its singularities control the isolated ordinary double points and its Euler stratification enters the Hodge-number computation. The source deliberately works with aggregate invariants without irreducibility. Splitting D into two irreducible genus-9 normalizations shows that the entire 96-node locus has a uniform global explanation as the transverse intersection of the two residual components, while all intrinsic singularity is concentrated in 32 cusps on each. This is a natural structural refinement of the discriminant geometry, not an arbitrary coefficient check.
